newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TASMANIA LOOK TO PONTING FOR RESCUE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TASMANIA LOOK TO PONTING FOR RESCUE.

text.p: Discarded Australia test batsman Ricky Ponting provided the only resistance for Tasmania as South Australia took a firm grip of their Sheffield Shield match on Wednesday.
After amassing a first innings total of 387 all out, South Australia reduced the home side to 136 for five at close of play on the second day at Hobart's Bellerive Oval.
Ponting, who was overlooked for Australia's tour to South Africa after being dropped during the recent home test series against West Indies, remained unbeaten on 76 after a top order collapse.
Tasmania captain David Boon, the batsman Ponting replaced as Australia's test number three, scored six to worsen his side's plight.

Tasmania, who will move into second place on the Sheffield Shield table behind Western Australia with an outright victory, need to score another 252 runs to earn two competition points for a first innings lead.
Resuming on 251 for five, South Australia frustrated their hosts during the morning session as Joe Scuderi and Tim Nielsen added 122 runs for the sixth wicket in better than even time.
All-rounder Scuderi scored 70 before returning later in the day to take two for 25 in five overs of medium pace.
